description: One minimal fixture per violation class, plus a clean baseline. Each fixture isolates exactly one class so an integration test can assert that class and nothing else.
conventions: Every fixture declares <html lang="en"> and a <title>, so html-has-lang / html-lang-valid / document-title never fire. fixture-no-lang.html breaks this on purpose.
All content sits inside a single <main>, so the best-practice `region` and `landmark-one-main` rules never fire.
Exactly one <h1> per fixture, so `page-has-heading-one` never fires.
Text is #1f2a33 on #ffffff (14.61:1) and links are #0b5a52 (8.08:1), so `color-contrast` never fires. fixture-low-contrast.html breaks this on purpose.
Buttons and inputs are >=48px and icon controls >=44px, so `target-size` never fires. fixture-target-size.html breaks this on purpose.
No positive tabindex, no animation and no fixed widths, except in the fixture testing each.
No background gradients or images anywhere, so axe can always resolve a background colour and returns pass/fail rather than incomplete.
The defect under test is marked with a DEFECT comment in the markup.

expectationFields.ruleIdOrCheck: axe-core rule ID, or an a11y-loop check name
expectationFields.scHint: WCAG 2.2 success criterion number that is the source of the obligation
expectationFields.level: conformance level of the success criterion
expectationFields.axeTag: the axe tag the rule carries, or null for a11y-loop checks. Rules tagged best-practice are filtered out of a WCAG-tag-scoped run and land in the separated non-blocking bucket.
expectationFields.minNodes: assert at least this many findings; tests should use >= rather than ==
expectationFields.allowNeedsReview: true if the finding may legitimately land in needsReview / incomplete rather than violations
expectationFields.requiresPass: the audit pass this finding needs: default, dark, forced-colors, reduced-motion, or viewport-320
expectationFields.requiresAxeOption: an axe run option the finding depends on
expectationFields.routedFrom: the severity the engine reported before a documented a11y-loop rule moved the row to needsReview; asserts the row carries routedFrom, note and noteUrl
expectationFields.mustNotReport: fixture-level: rule ids that must produce no row in ANY bucket (violations, needsReview or bestPractice). The guard for a check's known false-positive shape, which expectClean cannot express because it ignores needsReview.

assertAlso: For every fixture except the one under test, no other rule in the wcag2a/wcag2aa/wcag21a/wcag21aa/wcag22aa tag set should report a violation. A new finding in an unrelated fixture means either the fixture drifted or a runner regression.

verifiedAgainst.method: Served over http on 127.0.0.1 (never file://), axe.run with runOnly by tag and resultTypes ['violations','incomplete'], across the default / dark / forced-colors / reduced-motion / 320x256 passes, with the dialog fixtures also driven into their open state.
verifiedAgainst.note: Every expectation below was observed, not predicted. Where axe behaved differently from what the rule metadata suggested, the observed behaviour is what is recorded and the surprise is called out in the fixture's note.

axeBehaviourNotes: A tag-based runOnly ENABLES rules that ship with enabled:false. target-size carries enabled:false in axe-core 4.12.1, but running with runOnly {type:'tag', values:[...'wcag22aa']} reports it anyway. No explicit rules option is needed.

A placeholder is a valid fallback in the accessible name computation, so axe's `label` rule PASSES on placeholder-only inputs, and `label-title-only` does not fire either (it covers title, not placeholder). See fixture-placeholder-only-label.html.
aria-labelledby pointing at a nonexistent ID lands in `incomplete`, not `violations` — axe cannot be certain the reference is wrong.
linear-gradient backgrounds make color-contrast return incomplete with reason bgGradient. Text over a gradient is never passed or failed.

Elements extending beyond the viewport make color-contrast return incomplete with reason elmPartiallyObscured, and very short strings return shortTextContent. Both appear on otherwise-clean pages at the 320px pass and are expected.

Under forced-colors emulation, axe's color-contrast reports one incomplete result (1:1 computed ratio) on any real <button> element — observed on fixture-clean.html and nearly every other fixture with a button, including some with no other seeded defect at all. This is Chromium's forced-colors colour flattening defeating axe's contrast computation, not a fixture or runner problem. Integration tests must not assert zero needsReview results; only zero violations is meaningful.

fixture-clean.html.title: Fully accessible page
fixture-clean.html.note: Verified against the running CLI (a11y-loop build-cli-2, integration pass): zero violations in all five passes. NOT zero incomplete results, correcting this note's earlier claim: under forced-colors emulation, axe's color-contrast reports one incomplete result on button[type=submit] with a computed 1:1 ratio. See the top-level axeBehaviourNotes entry — this is a Chromium forced-colors interaction that affects any real <button> on any page, not a defect in this fixture. Zero violations is still the thing that means the runner is wrong if it ever fails here.

fixture-low-contrast.html.title: Text below the SC 1.4.3 contrast thresholds
fixture-low-contrast.html.note: Two pairs: #999999 on #ffffff (2.84:1) and #ffffff on #5fbfb2 (2.19:1). Both backgrounds are solid, so axe resolves them and reports violations. The highest-volume failure class in the wild: 83.9% of home pages, averaging 34 instances each.

fixture-missing-alt.html.title: Images with no text alternative
fixture-missing-alt.html.note: Three images: the first has alt text and must not be reported; the other two have no alt attribute.

fixture-unlabeled-input.html.title: Form controls with no programmatic label

expect.note: axe tags this rule wcag412; SC 1.3.1 and 3.3.2 are the other obligations. The rule's selector is `input, textarea`.
A separate rule from `label`, because `label` does not match select elements.

fixture-unlabeled-input.html.note: No name source at all — deliberately including no placeholder, because a placeholder makes axe's `label` rule pass. Observed: label(2) on the input and textarea, select-name(1) on the select, nothing else. See fixture-placeholder-only-label.html for the placeholder case.

fixture-placeholder-only-label.html.title: Placeholder standing in for a label — an axe coverage gap
fixture-placeholder-only-label.html.axeExpectation: ZERO violations. Verified: axe `label` PASSES on all three fields, and `label-title-only` does not fire. Assert this explicitly — it is the point of the fixture.
fixture-placeholder-only-label.html.note: A placeholder is a valid fallback name source in the accessible name computation, so a placeholder-only form is reported clean by axe even though it is the most common shape of the missing-label failure in generated markup. The label vanishes as soon as the field has content, is announced inconsistently, cannot be clicked to focus the field, and is usually styled at unreadable contrast. `placeholder-as-label` is a PROPOSED a11y-loop check — it is not in the agreed check list and the CLI does not implement it yet. If it is not adopted, this fixture still earns its place as a regression guard on the axe behaviour.

fixture-empty-link.html.title: Links with no accessible name
fixture-empty-link.html.note: Icon-only links wrapping an aria-hidden SVG. Sized at 44px so target-size does not also fire. SC 4.1.2 is the secondary obligation.

fixture-empty-button.html.title: Buttons with no accessible name
fixture-empty-button.html.note: One icon-only button, and one whose only text sits inside an aria-hidden span.

fixture-no-lang.html.title: Missing document language
fixture-no-lang.html.note: The `html-lang-valid` rule must NOT also fire: there is no lang attribute to be invalid.

fixture-div-button.html.title: Clickable div acting as a button
fixture-div-button.html.note: No axe rule fires on this fixture at all — assert zero axe violations alongside the a11y-loop findings. A div and a span, each with onclick, no role, no tabindex and no key handler. SC 4.1.2 is the secondary obligation. The archetypal AI-codegen failure.

fixture-heading-skip.html.title: Skipped heading levels
fixture-heading-skip.html.note: h1 then h3 then h5. Verified against axe-core 4.12.1 metadata: heading-order carries cat.semantics and best-practice only, with no wcag tag, so a WCAG-tag-scoped run will not surface it. Enable the best-practice tag to assert this fixture.

fixture-focus-invisible.html.title: Focus indicator removed with no replacement

expect.note: Corrected from an earlier 'focus-visibility' placeholder name to the actual implemented rule id. Observed: all three focusable elements (button, link, labelled input) each report focus-not-visible.

fixture-focus-invisible.html.note: A universal reset covering both :focus and :focus-visible, so no fallback survives. Three focusable elements are affected: a button, a link and a labelled input. No axe rule fires. Detection needs computed styles read in the focused state.

fixture-broken-aria.html.title: Broken and invalid ARIA

expect.note: aria-labelledby pointing at an ID that does not exist. Observed in axe-core 4.12.1: this lands in `incomplete`, NOT `violations` — assert it there. `button-name` correctly does not fire, because the name falls back to the text content.
role="heading" with no aria-level.
aria-hidden on a focusable link. Breaks rule 4 of the four rules of ARIA use.
role="menu" with no owned menuitems. Observed as a violation on `ul`. The clearest 'a role is a promise' case on any fixture: the whole APG Menu keyboard contract is implied and none of it exists.

Not seeded separately — this is the same root cause. Putting role="menu" on the ul strips the list role from its parent, so the li elements are no longer contained in a list and axe reports each one. Recorded here so an integration test asserting 'nothing else fires' does not trip over it.

fixture-broken-aria.html.note: Four seeded defects across four rules, plus `listitem` as a knock-on of the role="menu" defect. Broken ARIA references are documented as an emergent failure mode specific to LLM-generated code, and pages using ARIA average more errors than pages without it. Observed: aria-required-attr(1), aria-hidden-focus(1), aria-required-children(1), listitem(2) as violations; aria-valid-attr-value(1) as incomplete.

fixture-modal-no-trap.html.title: Modal dialog with no focus management

expect.note: Corrected from a single placeholder 'dialog-focus-trap' entry to the three actual rule ids the dialog check emits. dialog-focus-not-returned does NOT fire here: it only evaluates once Escape has actually closed the dialog, and here it never does.

steps: click #openDialog
wait for #fakeDialog to have class "open"
run the audit with the dialog open
interact.note: This is the state-coverage fixture. On load the dialog is display:none and absent from the accessibility tree, so an audit that only runs on page load reports a completely clean page. Every finding exists only in the open state. The companion fixture-modal-no-trap.interact.mjs exports states['modal-open'], a Playwright page callback performing exactly the two steps above.

defects: no focus moved into the dialog on open
no focus trap: Tab walks out into the page behind
Escape does nothing — no keydown listener anywhere
focus is not returned to the trigger on close
background content is neither inert nor aria-hidden
fixture-modal-no-trap.html.note: The dialog is deliberately given an accessible name via aria-label, a real <button> close control with a name, and a labelled input, so focus management is the only defect. `aria-dialog-name` must NOT fire.

fixture-portalled-dialog.html.title: A CORRECT portalled dialog — the shape :modal does not match

expect.note: Not a seeded defect, and not something the fixture could avoid: it is what the portal pattern itself costs. Two of the three are the focus guards, which are focusable AND aria-hidden by design (Base UI ships exactly this); the third is the page behind the sheet, hidden from assistive technology with aria-hidden rather than inert. Observed in axe-core 4.12.1 as incomplete, not violations - axe cannot determine focusability here and says so.

steps: click #openMenu
wait for [data-portal] [role="dialog"]
run the audit with the sheet open
interact.note: There is no dialog in the document at all until the menu is opened - it is portalled in on click, as the last child of <body>.

fixture-portalled-dialog.html.note: The INVERSE of fixture-modal-no-trap.html: this dialog's focus management is correct in every respect, so no a11y-loop dialog or keyboard rule may fire on it. It is a regression guard for the survey root, not for a defect. Before the fix, tabbableRoot() was "document.querySelector(':modal') || document.body", and :modal matches ONLY a native <dialog> opened with showModal(). This dialog is a portalled <div role="dialog"> with no aria-modal attribute, hiding the page behind it with aria-hidden on its siblings - the shape Base UI, Radix, Headless UI and everything else built on floating-ui ships, and the currently recommended pattern. So the root fell back to document.body and the survey put its focus sentinel at body.firstChild: outside the open dialog, in the one region the focus trap exists to keep focus out of. Measured on this fixture at 0.2.4, three runs, identical every time: keyboard-unreachable(3) on the start guard, on the link behind the sheet and on the trigger, plus dialog-focus-not-trapped(1) on the sheet, plus focus-order-diverges(1) in needsReview. All five are artifacts of the survey, not of the page. The guards hand focus back on the NEXT Tab rather than one animation frame later, which is what floating-ui's enqueueFocus does. Same shape and the same code path - focus rests outside the dialog for exactly one tick - but a keypress is deterministic where a frame is a race, and a fixture that reproduced the bug only sometimes would prove nothing. See the fixture's own comments.

fixture-target-size.html.title: Targets below 24 by 24 CSS px

expect.note: Corrected from 'target-size' (which collides with the axe rule id below) to the actual a11y-loop rule id, and allowNeedsReview corrected to true: this check is always needs-review by design, never a violation, because the SC's Equivalent/User agent/Essential exceptions cannot be judged mechanically.

The rule ships with enabled:false in axe-core 4.12.1, but a tag-based runOnly turns it on: running with runOnly {type:'tag', values:[...'wcag22aa']} reported target-size(3) with no explicit rules option. Observed both ways, same result. allowNeedsReview stays true because the SC's spacing and inline exceptions are hard to evaluate mechanically and a11y-loop reports this as needs-review by design.

fixture-target-size.html.note: Three 16x16 buttons with 4px spacing, so neither the size requirement nor the 24px offset alternative is met. All three have aria-label names, so geometry is the only defect. display:flex rather than inline-flex keeps them out of axe's inline-widget exception.

fixture-reflow-overflow.html.title: Fixed width forcing horizontal scroll

expect.note: Corrected from 'reflow-overflow' to the actual implemented rule id.

fixture-reflow-overflow.html.note: A 1200px panel. Detected by measuring document scrollWidth against clientWidth at 320x256, the viewport WCAG specifies for the 400% zoom reflow test. The finding should name the overflowing element (.wide). No axe rule fires; assert zero axe violations.

fixture-reduced-motion.html.title: Infinite animation ignoring motion preference

expect.note: Corrected from 'reduced-motion' to the actual implemented rule id.

fixture-reduced-motion.html.note: Infinite animation, no pause control, no prefers-reduced-motion block. SC 2.2.2 (Level A) is the primary citation because the motion starts automatically and runs beyond five seconds; SC 2.3.3 (AAA) is secondary. Verified behaviourally: re-run with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce emulated and confirm the element has stopped moving, rather than checking that a media query exists.

fixture-ambiguous-links.html.title: Link text that conveys no purpose

expect.note: Corrected from 'ambiguous-link' to the actual implemented rule id, and allowNeedsReview corrected to true: this heuristic is always needs-review by design (SC 2.4.4 permits vague text when context supplies the purpose, which only a human can judge), so it never lands in violations. This fixture has zero violations of any kind — that is expected, not a runner failure.

fixture-ambiguous-links.html.note: "click here", "Read more", "here", "Learn more". One descriptive link is present and must not be reported. This check is a heuristic and should be reported as such — it cannot judge whether a longer name is descriptive enough, which stays on the manual checklist.

fixture-positive-tabindex.html.title: Positive tabindex reordering the tab sequence

expect.note: Corrected from a placeholder 'tab-order' entry. Both tabindex="1" and tabindex="2" elements are reported directly. The tab-order-diff walk (focus-order-diverges / keyboard-unreachable) deliberately does NOT also fire on these two elements: a positive-tabindex element sorts into an earlier phase of the browser's focus order than a forward-only walk anchored at document start can ever reach, so the walk cannot observe it — reporting it as "unreachable" there would double-count the same defect under a second, misleading rule id. positive-tabindex is the correct and only a11y-loop detector for this fixture.

Verified against axe-core 4.12.1 metadata: tags are cat.keyboard and best-practice only, with no wcag tag, so a WCAG-tag-scoped run will not surface it. SC 2.4.3 is still the obligation; axe simply does not assert the mapping.

fixture-positive-tabindex.html.note: tabindex="1" and tabindex="2" on the last two controls, pulling them to the front of the document's tab order ahead of a link and a button that precede them visually.

fixture-forced-colors-dark-surface.html.title: Light text on a dark surface, read by axe under forced colors

expect.note: Not a seeded defect: #e8e6ef on #141218 is 15.04:1 and silent in every other pass. Under forced-colors emulation axe reads -webkit-text-fill-color (the author's #e8e6ef) against the forced #ffffff and reports 1.23:1 as a violation. Up to 0.3.2 that one row made this page exit 1. a11y-loop now routes color-contrast from the forced-colors pass to needsReview with a note pointing at the Field Note, so the page exits 0 and the row is still reported. The #6d6975 paragraph (5.34:1) is the control: dark-on-light text survives the same comparison and produces no row.

fixture-forced-colors-dark-surface.html.note: Regression target for the forced-colors routing in findingsFromAxeResult. Measured 2026-10-20 at axe-core 4.14.0: on 0.3.2 this fixture reported one violation and exited 1; with the routing it reports zero violations, one needsReview row, and exits 0.

fixture-dialog-submit-inside.html.title: A CORRECT dialog whose own Submit button a state clicks

steps: submit-invalid: click #openSub, click the dialog's own #submitSub with the field empty; the dialog stays open with an error, and the Escape probe then closes it
submit-valid: click #openSub, fill the field, click #submitSub; the state's own action closes the dialog
reopen-from-script: submit-valid, then showModal() from script with no new activation outside the dialog

fixture-dialog-submit-inside.html.note: Regression guard for the dialog-focus-not-returned false positive in evals/benchmark-results.md (2026-10). Up to 0.3.x the trigger was the presumed trigger, the last clicked element read when the probe ran, which in the submit-invalid state is the dialog's own Submit button, so the Escape probe expected focus to return to Submit and reported the dialog when it correctly went to Subscribe. The state recorder in src/lib/browser-utils.js now takes the opener at the moment the dialog opens. Measured 2026-10-20: with every state forced back onto the presumed-trigger fall-back, submit-invalid reports dialog-focus-not-returned (violation, inferred); with the fix no state reports a row. The inside-the-dialog filter in pickOpener is guarded separately by reopen-from-script, where the most recent activation is the dialog's own Submit: with the filter removed, that state reports the row (measured 2026-10-20 for the PR #39 review).

fixture-dialog-focus-lost.html.title: A dialog closed by its own Submit drops focus to the body

expect.note: Reported by closedDialogFindings, not by the Escape probe: no dialog is open when the state returns, so the probe never runs. The opener is still on the page, so both rows are violations, evidence inferred. submit-then-click guards the freeze: each close is judged from a focus snapshot taken when focus lands or the 1 s settle window ends, and frozen by the state's next activation. With the freeze disabled the snapshot settles on Help and that state reports nothing (measured 2026-10-20).

steps: submit-valid: click #openSub, fill #subEmail, click #submitSub, which removes the dialog
submit-then-click: the same, then click #help, which puts focus on Help

defects: the dialog is removed with focus inside it and focus is not returned to the opener
fixture-dialog-focus-lost.html.note: The inverse of fixture-dialog-submit-inside.html: the same click on the dialog's own Submit, but focus really is lost.

fixture-route-focus-lost.html.title: A client-side route change drops focus to the body

steps: click the Order 1042 link; the page's router pushes /orders/1042 and replaces <main>

defects: the focused link is removed with the old view and nothing moves focus to the new one
fixture-route-focus-lost.html.note: The new view's text is a route change, not a status message, so status-message-not-announced must not fire on it.

fixture-route-focus-managed.html.title: A CORRECT client-side route change that moves focus to the new heading

steps: click the Order 1042 link; the router pushes /orders/1042, replaces <main> and focuses the new h1

fixture-status-not-announced.html.title: A status message outside any live region

expect.note: A violation, evidence inferred, because every confidence signal is present: the text is short, reads like a status ("Saved"), and appeared in the same form as the button the state pressed.

steps: click #save, which appends a plain paragraph to the form

defects: the confirmation is a plain paragraph, not in a live region, and focus stays on the button

fixture-status-announced.html.title: A CORRECT status message, and a disclosure that is not one

steps: saved: click #save, which writes into a role="status" region that was in the page from the start
details-expanded: click the aria-expanded disclosure, which reveals its aria-controls target
discount-applied: click Apply member discount; a short note appears next to the button and the page moves focus to the Order total heading

fixture-status-announced.html.note: Passing counterpart of fixture-status-not-announced.html, plus the disclosure exclusion: the revealed paragraph contains the word "Saved" on purpose, so it is the aria-controls relationship, not the wording, that keeps it from being reported. discount-applied guards the focus-moved-by-the-page exclusion: with it removed, that state reports one needsReview row (measured 2026-10-20).

fixture-live-region-late.html.title: A live region inserted already holding its text

expect.note: Always needsReview: the region carries the right role, and whether its initial content is announced depends on the browser and screen reader.

steps:
click #addToCart, which appends
Added to cart.
in one mutation

defects: the live region and its text are inserted in the same mutation batch
fixture-live-region-late.html.note: expectClean is true because the row is needs-review: the page has no violation, and exits 0.

fixture-dialog-sequences.html.title: CORRECT dialogs driven through sequences an end-of-state reading gets wrong

steps: submit-then-click-text: open Rename, Save (focus returns to Rename), then click plain text (Chromium moves focus to <body>)
keyboard-open: open with Enter, Save with Space
two-in-a-row: Rename then Invite, each returning focus to its opener
delete-row: the opener is removed with its row and focus goes to the Members heading
late-return: a <div role="dialog"> that hides and restores focus to its opener 300 ms later

fixture-dialog-sequences.html.note: From the PR #39 review repros (2026-10-20). Measured: judging each close from focus at the end of the state reports submit-then-click-text; a settle window of 0 reports late-return. Chromium's native <dialog>.close() restores focus synchronously, which is why the late-return dialog is a custom one.

fixture-dialog-opener-removed.html.title: A dialog removes its own opener and leaves focus on the body

expect.note: Opener gone and focus on <body>: a violation, evidence inferred. Opener gone and focus on a sensible element is silent (the delete-row state of fixture-dialog-sequences.html). An unknown opener is needsReview.

steps: click Delete Ana and confirm; the row and its opener are removed and focus is left on <body>

defects: the opener is removed with its row and focus is not moved anywhere

fixture-error-summary.html.title: CORRECT validation: error summary, first invalid field, linked inline errors

steps: govuk-summary: submit empty; the error summary is shown and focused, and each inline error is linked from its field by aria-describedby
focus-first-invalid: submit empty; focus moves to the first invalid field
blur-validation: type a bad address and Tab on; the error appears, linked from its field

fixture-error-summary.html.note: From the PR #39 review repros (2026-10-20): before the fix, govuk-summary reported two violations and focus-first-invalid one. Those two states are now excluded because the page moved focus somewhere other than the activated control. blur-validation is the state that depends on the exclusion for text any element names with aria-describedby or aria-errormessage: with it removed, that state reports one needsReview row (measured 2026-10-20).

fixture-route-shadow-announcer.html.title: CORRECT client-side routes: a shadow-root announcer, and focus after a fetch

steps: shadow-announcer: follow the order link; the route is announced in an aria-live region inside an open shadow root, the way the Next.js App Router does it
focus-after-fetch: follow the order link; the new h1 is focused 300 ms later

fixture-route-shadow-announcer.html.note: From the PR #39 review repros (2026-10-20). Measured: collecting live regions from the light DOM only reports shadow-announcer; judging focus without the 1 s settle reports focus-after-fetch.

fixture-query-state.html.title: Filter state in the query string, with an unannounced result count

expect.note: A violation, evidence inferred: "2 results" is short, reads like a status and appears next to the button.

steps: click Show red only; the list filters in place, replaceState writes ?color=red, and "2 results" is appended next to the button

defects: the result count is a plain paragraph, outside any live region
fixture-query-state.html.note: From the PR #39 review (2026-10-20). A changed query string or an unmatched hash counts as a route change only when <main> was replaced as well. Measured: counting the query string alone as a route stands the status-message check down, and this fixture then reports nothing.
